title: LA Galaxy finalizing deal to sign Chucky Lozano on loan from San Diego FC: Sources
content:
The LA Galaxy are finalizing a deal to sign out-of-favor Mexican winger Hirving “Chucky” Lozano on loan from San Diego FC, multiple sources briefed on the situation tell The Athletic.

Lozano is set to become a designated player for the Galaxy, and while San Diego gave permission to Lozano to negotiate with the Galaxy, it would still be on the hook for a portion of his salary, sources add. ESPN Mexico first reported the talks.

Lozano hasn’t featured for San Diego in 2026 and has been training alone all season after the club decided he wasn’t part of its plans, just a year after making Lozano the face of its expansion season. According to the most recent MLS Players Association figures, his $9.33 million in guaranteed compensation in 2026 makes him the fourth-highest-paid player in MLS. He trails only Lionel Messi, Son Heung-min and Rodrigo De Paul in that department.

For Lozano, a potential move to the Galaxy represents a chance at a fresh start. The 31-year-old winger has been productive in his MLS minutes, with nine goals and 10 assists in 27 regular-season matches last season (1,833 minutes) and another two goals and an assist in four playoff games off the bench. He would join a remade Galaxy attack, which has included the club selling Gabriel Pec for a record fee to Cruzeiro, while Japanese forward Kyōgo Furuhashi has joined from Birmingham.

Lozano’s time in San Diego has been effectively over since the offseason. San Diego sporting director Tyler Heaps said in January that Lozano “wasn’t part of the team’s plans,” and he has been separated from the group since. First public signs of discontent emerged last October, when Lozano was omitted from the club’s squad for its season finale vs. Portland. The Athletic reported that the decision stemmed from a locker-room altercation earlier in the month following a halftime substitution that angered the player.

Earlier this summer, San Diego signed Tunisian winger Elias Achouri to a DP deal, and Heaps was asked again about Lozano.

“Nothing has changed from our side,” Heaps said. “A lot of it depends on him and his decision, if he wants to continue to play football.”
